result.title: When Planning Problems Become Hard for LLMs: Separating Structural Complexity from Semantic Interpretability
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) struggle with classical planning, but benchmarks rarely distinguish structural difficulty from the difficulty of interpreting symbolic vocabulary. We examine seven STRIPS domains with BFS-optimal plan lengths. For predicting structural difficulty without solving an instance, the zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic $h_{\mathrm{add}}$ outperforms learned alternatives on held-out domains (mean Spearman $|ρ|=0.931$), including ridge regression ($0.707$), object count ($0.657$), and the episodic retrieval architecture ARC ($0.400$). ARC also fails to outperform a linear model using the same features. To isolate semantic effects, we progressively rename predicates while preserving states, transitions, and optimal plans. Valid LLM planning success drops from $67.5\%$ to $40.0\%$ between $0\%$ and $100\%$ renaming, while refusals remain at $0\%$. An LLM supplied with ARC's conditioning information predicts difficulty in context better than trained ARC (mean $|ρ|=0.826$). Hybrid routing between an LLM and a symbolic planner depends more on calibration to the target LLM's outcomes than on the structural score selected. Thus, established symbolic heuristics already estimate structural difficulty well; improving hybrid planning requires modeling LLM behavior sensitive to predicate semantics rather than developing more structural predictors.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在七个 STRIPS 规划域中比较零训练的 delete-relaxation 启发式 h_add 与回归、对象计数、ARC 检索等学习式方法对实例结构难度的预测能力，并通过逐步重命名谓词（保持状态与最优解不变）来分离语义可解释性对 LLM 规划成功率的影响，最后考察 LLM 与符号规划器之间的混合路由。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「结构难度 vs 语义可解释性」的区分与路由校准分析，可能为 LVR 中判断失败源自内部状态表示还是表面证据接地、以及何时调用额外计算或符号工具提供可核查线索，但需确认能否迁移到视觉多模态场景。
